frontmatter.description: It enables developers to automate slide generation, modification, and conversion workflows directly in Python without requiring Microsoft PowerPoint.
frontmatter.title: Use Cases

blocks.content: Aspose.Slides FOSS is the official open-source Python library for creating, reading, and editing PowerPoint (.pptx) presentations. It enables developers to automate slide generation, modification, and conversion workflows directly in Python without requiring Microsoft PowerPoint.

The library supports rich text formatting through `TextFrame`, `Paragraph`, and `Portion` objects—including bullets, character styles, and paragraph alignment—as well as advanced 3D effects like bevels, cameras, light rigs, materials, and extrusion depth. This makes it suitable for generating dynamic reports, educational materials, and presentation templates programmatically.

import aspose_slides_foss as slides
from aspose_slides_foss import SaveFormat

# Create a new presentation
with slides.Presentation() as prs:
    slide = prs.slides[0]
    prs.save("new.pptx", SaveFormat.PPTX)

Aspose.Slides for Python enables developers to programmatically create, modify, and save PowerPoint presentations with full fidelity to the .pptx format. The library loads existing presentations into an in-memory object model, allowing precise manipulation of slides, shapes, text, and formatting before saving back to disk. This round-trip capability ensures that presentations retain their structure and visual integrity across save operations, making it ideal for automated report generation, template-based slide creation, and batch slide processing in production workflows.

Shape formatting is handled through a structured API that supports multiple fill types—including solid, gradient, pattern, and picture fills—via the `FillFormat` object. Developers can set fill properties directly on shapes or text portions, and the library preserves these settings when saving to .pptx. This level of control supports consistent branding, dynamic styling, and rich visual content generation in slides python workflows.

from aspose_slides_foss import ShapeType, FillType
from aspose_slides_foss import Color
import aspose_slides_foss as slides
from aspose_slides_foss import SaveFormat

with slides.Presentation() as prs:
    shape = prs.slides[0].shapes.add_auto_shape(ShapeType.RECTANGLE, 50, 50, 300, 150)
    shape.fill_format.fill_type = FillType.SOLID
    shape.fill_format.solid_fill_color.color = Color.from_argb(255, 30, 120, 200)
    prs.save("fill.pptx", SaveFormat.PPTX)

This example demonstrates how to manage per-slide notes and add a table with header text using Aspose.Slides. It shows how to create a notes slide for speaker content and insert a table with formatted header cells — both essential for building professional presentation decks programmatically in Python.

import aspose_slides_foss

# Create a new presentation
presentation = aspose_slides_foss.Presentation()
slide = presentation.slides[0]

# Add speaker notes for the slide
notes = slide.notes_slide_manager.add_notes_slide()
notes.notes_text_frame.text = "Speaker notes here."

# Add a 3x2 table with header row
col_widths = [120.0, 120.0, 120.0]
row_heights = [40.0, 40.0]
x, y = 50.0, 100.0
table = slide.shapes.add_table(x, y, col_widths, row_heights)
table.rows[0][0].text_frame.text = "Header"

Aspose.Slides for Python via .NET enables developers to create, manipulate, and convert PowerPoint files programmatically. With support for rich shape types, visual effects, and threaded comments, it serves as a robust solution for generating dynamic presentations in Python slides for beginners and enterprise use cases alike.
